AggregateValue#summary.en: What the function of {@link aggregate} returns for a group: a number, an array of numbers, or named numbers.

DataFrame#summary.en: A data frame: an object of columns of equal length. `null` (and `NaN` in a numeric column) is a missing value.

DataRow#summary.en: A row of a data frame, as passed to the condition of {@link subset}: column name to value.

DataValue#summary.en: One value of a data frame column (`null`: missing).

FromRowsOptions.columns#summary.en:
The columns to take, in this order. Default: every key that occurs in some row, in the order of first
appearance.

GroupingLabels#summary.en: The group labels of the rows: one per row.

GroupingLevel#summary.en: A level of a grouping factor (a label that is not missing).

MergeOptions.all#summary.en: Keep the rows of both frames that have no match. Default `false`.

MergeOptions.allX#summary.en: Keep the rows of x that have no match in y (y's columns missing). Default `all`.

MergeOptions.allY#summary.en: Keep the rows of y that have no match in x (x's columns missing). Default `all`.

MergeOptions.by#summary.en: The key columns, in both frames. Default: the column names common to both, in x's order.

MergeOptions.byX#summary.en: The key columns of x. Default `by`.

MergeOptions.byY#summary.en: The key columns of y (as many as `byX`, matched in order). Default `by`.

MergeOptions.sort#summary.en: Order the rows by the key. Default `true`.

MergeOptions.suffixes#summary.en: Appended to the names of the non-key columns that occur in both frames. Default `[".x", ".y"]`.

MissingVector#summary.en: A vector: numbers (`NaN` missing), or strings, booleans or numbers with `null` for a missing value.

PivotLongerOptions#summary.en: Options for {@link pivotLonger} (tidyr's arguments in camelCase).

PivotLongerOptions.cols#summary.en: The columns to pivot: their names, in this order, or a test of the name (selecting in the data's order).

PivotLongerOptions.colsVary#summary.en:
`"fastest"` (default): the pivoted columns vary within each input row; `"slowest"`: all rows for each column in
turn. Any other value is an error, as in tidyr.

PivotLongerOptions.namesPattern#summary.en: A regular expression whose capture groups are the parts of the names.

PivotLongerOptions.namesPrefix#summary.en: A regular expression whose match at the start of the names is removed.

PivotLongerOptions.namesSep#summary.en: A regular expression at whose matches the names are split into the parts.

PivotLongerOptions.namesTo#summary.en:
The columns to make from the names, one per part of the names. `".value"` marks the part that names the value
columns. With `[]`, no columns are made from the names (namesSep and namesPattern are not used). Default `"name"`.

PivotLongerOptions.namesTransform#summar.en:
Functions applied to the parts, by `namesTo` column (the part as a string; missing parts stay missing). Own
properties only: a `namesTo` column named toString has no transform unless one is given. The transform of
`".value"` gives the names of the value columns, and must return strings.

PivotLongerOptions.onWarning#summary.en:
Called with each of tidyr's warnings, once per distinct warning, in order. Default: the warnings go to the handler
of {@link setWarningHandler} (none by default).

PivotLongerOptions.valuesDropNa#summary.en: Drop the rows where every value column is missing. Default `false`.

PivotLongerOptions.valuesTo#summary.en: The name of the value column (without `".value"` in `namesTo`). Default `"value"`.

PivotSummary#summary.en: A summary of the values of one cell (in data order), for `valuesFn` of {@link pivotWider}.

PivotWiderOptions#summary.en: Options for {@link pivotWider} (tidyr's arguments in camelCase).

PivotWiderOptions.idCols#summary.en:
The columns that identify a row of the result. Default: every column not in `namesFrom` or `valuesFrom`, in the
data's order; when given, the other columns are dropped (a column of `namesFrom` or `valuesFrom` is an error).

PivotWiderOptions.namesFrom#summary.en: The column (or columns) whose values name the new columns (at least one). Default `"name"`.

PivotWiderOptions.namesPrefix#summary.en: Put before each new name. Default `""`.

PivotWiderOptions.namesSep#summary.en: Joins the values of several `namesFrom` columns, and a value column's name to the name. Default `"_"`.

PivotWiderOptions.namesSort#summary.en: Sort the names (by the first `namesFrom` column, then the next) instead of taking them in order of appearance.

PivotWiderOptions.namesVary#summary.en:
With several `valuesFrom`: `"fastest"` (default) all names for each value column; `"slowest"` each value column
for each name. Any other value is an error, as in tidyr.

PivotWiderOptions.valuesFill#summary.en:
The value of a cell that no row fills, or such values by value column. Default: missing. As in tidyr, it is cast
to the type of the value column: a boolean becomes 0 or 1 in a numeric column, 0 and 1 become false and true in a
boolean column (NaN missing); any other mix (a string with a number or a boolean) is an error.

PivotWiderOptions.valuesFn#summary.en:
Summarises the values of each filled cell, or such functions by value column. As in tidyr, the results for one
value column take one common type: booleans become 0 and 1 if any result is a number; strings mixed with numbers
or booleans are an error.

PivotWiderOptions.valuesFrom#summary.en: The column (or columns) whose values fill the new columns (at least one). Default `"value"`.

SplitOptions.drop#summary.en: With several factors, leave out the combinations without a row. Default `false`.

SplitOptions.sep#summary.en: The separator of the levels in the names of combinations. Default `"."`.

SubsetOptions.select#summary.en: The columns to keep, in this order. Default: all, in their order.

TapplyResult.dim#summary.en: The number of levels of each factor.

TapplyResult.dimnames#summary.en: The levels of each factor (numbers as numbers).

TapplyResult.values#summary.en:
The cells in column-major order (the first factor varies fastest). When the function gave a single number for
every non-empty cell, numbers with NaN for the empty cells; otherwise the function's results, `null` for the
empty cells.

aggregate(0)#summary.en:
The function applied to the values of each group, as a data frame. Equivalent to R's `aggregate()`.

Formula form, `aggregate(formula, data, fun)`: `"y ~ g"`, `"y ~ g + h"`, `"cbind(y, z) ~ g"` or `". ~ g"` (every
column not on the right). The grouping variables are all the variables of the right-hand side in order of first
appearance, whatever its operators (`"y ~ g:h"` and `"y ~ g * h"` group by g and h); `"y ~ ."` groups by every
column not summarised, and `"y ~ 1"` gives one row without a grouping column. The rows with a missing value in any
variable of the formula are dropped first. Data frame form, `aggregate(x, by, fun)`: the columns of `x` summarised
by the label columns of `by` (its keys name them); only the rows with a missing label are dropped, so `fun` sees the
missing values of `x`.

The result has the grouping columns first (with the labels as in the data), then one column per summarised column,
and one row per non-empty combination of the groups (the first factor varying fastest). When `fun` returns k > 1
values, a summarised column `y` becomes `y.1`, ..., `y.k` (an array) or `y.<name>` (an object of numbers).

aggregate(1)#summary.en:
The function applied to the values of each group, as a data frame. Equivalent to R's `aggregate()`.

Formula form, `aggregate(formula, data, fun)`: `"y ~ g"`, `"y ~ g + h"`, `"cbind(y, z) ~ g"` or `". ~ g"` (every
column not on the right). The grouping variables are all the variables of the right-hand side in order of first
appearance, whatever its operators (`"y ~ g:h"` and `"y ~ g * h"` group by g and h); `"y ~ ."` groups by every
column not summarised, and `"y ~ 1"` gives one row without a grouping column. The rows with a missing value in any
variable of the formula are dropped first. Data frame form, `aggregate(x, by, fun)`: the columns of `x` summarised
by the label columns of `by` (its keys name them); only the rows with a missing label are dropped, so `fun` sees the
missing values of `x`.

The result has the grouping columns first (with the labels as in the data), then one column per summarised column,
and one row per non-empty combination of the groups (the first factor varying fastest). When `fun` returns k > 1
values, a summarised column `y` becomes `y.1`, ..., `y.k` (an array) or `y.<name>` (an object of numbers).

completeCases#@param args.en: Data frames (objects of equal-length columns) or arrays, all with the same number of rows.

completeCases#summary.en:
Which rows have no missing value. Equivalent to R's `complete.cases()`. One boolean per row, true when no column
of any argument is missing (`null`, or `NaN` in a numeric column) in that row.

fromRows#summary.en:
A data frame (an object of columns) from an array of row objects, the usual shape of JSON and of parsed CSV:
`[{ age: 30, score: 5 }, { age: 41, score: 7 }]` becomes `{ age: [30, 41], score: [5, 7] }`. A key that a row
lacks, and `undefined`, become `null` (a missing value). Values must be numbers, strings, booleans or `null`, and
one column may not mix numbers, strings and booleans. Not an R function. R reads data as data frames directly.

merge#summary.en:
Join two data frames on key columns. Equivalent to R's `merge()`. For data frames: every pair of rows of x and y
with equal keys (missing keys match each other; key columns of different types are compared in their common type,
as R's match: text, or numbers with TRUE as 1), and with `allX` / `allY` the rows without a match. Columns: the
keys (named as in x; in the common type when rows only in y are kept), x's other columns, y's other columns; a
non-key name present in both gets the suffixes. Rows are
ordered by the key unless `sort` is false (several keys: as text joined with "\r" unless `allX` or `allY`, as R
does); without key columns, the cross join (x varying fastest).

naOmit(0)#summary.en: The values that are not missing. Equivalent to R's `na.omit()`. For a vector.

naOmit(1)#summary.en: The values that are not missing. Equivalent to R's `na.omit()`. For a vector.

naOmit(2)#summary.en: The complete rows of a data frame, as R's `na.omit()` for a data frame: the same columns, in order, restricted to the rows where none is missing (`null`, or `NaN` in a numeric column); see {@link completeCases}.

pivotLonger#summary.en:
Reshapes a data frame from wide to long: the selected columns become rows. Equivalent to `tidyr::pivot_longer()` in
R. The result has the columns not selected, a column per part of the selected names (`namesTo`), and the value
column (`valuesTo`), or with `".value"` in `namesTo` one value column per value of that part. The values of the
selected columns are combined into one type: numbers with booleans give numbers; strings with either are an error.

pivotWider#summary.en:
Reshapes a data frame from long to wide: the values of `namesFrom` become columns, filled from `valuesFrom`.
Equivalent to `tidyr::pivot_wider()` in R. One row per combination of the id columns (in order of first appearance),
the new columns in order of first appearance of their names (unless `namesSort`). A cell that no row fills is
`valuesFill` (default missing). A cell that several rows fill is an error unless `valuesFn` summarises the values
(tidyr makes a list column there, which a data frame here cannot hold).

split(0)#summary.en:
The values of `x` (or the rows of a data frame) divided into groups. Equivalent to R's `split(x, f, drop, sep)`.

`f` is one array of group labels or an array of such arrays, one per factor. The result is a `Map` from the group's
name to its values, in R's order: with one factor its levels; with several every combination of their levels (the
first factor varying fastest), named by joining the levels with `sep`, the empty ones included unless `drop`.
Values whose label is missing are left out.

split(1)#summary.en:
The values of `x` (or the rows of a data frame) divided into groups. Equivalent to R's `split(x, f, drop, sep)`.

`f` is one array of group labels or an array of such arrays, one per factor. The result is a `Map` from the group's
name to its values, in R's order: with one factor its levels; with several every combination of their levels (the
first factor varying fastest), named by joining the levels with `sep`, the empty ones included unless `drop`.
Values whose label is missing are left out.

split(2)#summary.en:
The values of `x` (or the rows of a data frame) divided into groups. Equivalent to R's `split(x, f, drop, sep)`.

`f` is one array of group labels or an array of such arrays, one per factor. The result is a `Map` from the group's
name to its values, in R's order: with one factor its levels; with several every combination of their levels (the
first factor varying fastest), named by joining the levels with `sep`, the empty ones included unless `drop`.
Values whose label is missing are left out.

subset#summary.en:
The rows of a data frame that meet a condition, and optionally some of its columns. Equivalent to R's `subset()`.
For a data frame: `keep` is a boolean per row or a function of the row; a missing (`null`) or non-boolean result
counts as false, as R drops the rows whose condition is NA.

tapply#summary.en:
The function applied to the values of each group. Equivalent to R's `tapply(x, index, fun)`.

`index` is one array of group labels (one per value of `x`) or an array of such arrays, one per factor. The
function is called only for the non-empty cells; a value of `x` whose label is missing is left out.
